Spent some time on this from the code side. Findings, in case they help narrow it down:

Ruled out with evidence:

- Boot failure retry loop: LayerMap/RcMap in effect 4.0.0-beta.83 cache a failed location build for the whole 60 minute idle TTL, they do not retry per request. Verified empirically against the same effect version.
- Teardown fiber leak: the `agent.updated` / `command.updated` / `catalog.updated` emissions you observed at expiry are the `State.create` scope finalizers themselves (`state.ts` finalize), so location scope close provably runs. Boot emits the same three events when the state nodes first materialize.
- The `.updated` to refetch to reacquire cycle is client driven and quiesces once the RcMap entry is warm; a warm get is a cache hit.
- All literal spin constructs in core/server (while(true), Schedule.forever) block on queues or terminate. The session run coordinator goes fully quiescent when no wake is pending. Server SSE feed subscribers use dropping queues (4096) and self evict on overflow.

Still standing, and it matches your "state accumulated across expiry/reboot cycles" observation: subscriber accumulation on the two process global unbounded PubSubs in `packages/core/src/event.ts` (`pubsub.live` and the per type map, which is never pruned). Location scoped services subscribe to these global pubsubs from at least 8 call sites. One concrete path with no guaranteed unsubscribe is the plugin bridge in `packages/core/src/plugin/promise.ts`, which hands plugins `Stream.toAsyncIterable(events.subscribe())`; if the async iterator is never returned/closed, that generation's subscriber survives on the global pubsub. At N leaked subscribers every published event fans out to N unbounded queues, which would show up exactly as steady JS allocation churn.

If you can still reach a degraded server, dumping the subscriber counts of `pubsub.live` and `pubsub.typed` and comparing them against the number of live locations would confirm or kill that theory quickly.

While digging I also found a separate correctness bug in the same lifecycle: a location whose boot fails once serves the cached failure for the full 60 minute TTL with no recovery path (production never calls `locations.invalidate`). Filed as #38405 with a repro, fix in #38406.

experienced this in 1.18.4. The work around was not effective. I had to clean the db.

Following up on my earlier analysis: I can now reproduce the accumulation mechanism deterministically in about 4 seconds.

Setup: a promise plugin that consumes `ctx.event.subscribe()` in a detached `for await` loop and never closes the iterator, which is a normal thing for a real plugin to do. Cycle a location through boot then invalidate (invalidate exercises the same entry scope close as the 60 minute idle expiry) and count subscribers on the process global `pubsub.live` in `packages/core/src/event.ts` (the internal `subscribers` set size).

Results over 10 cycles:

- Control, no plugins: subscriber count returns to 0 after every cycle. The base location lifecycle cleans up correctly.
- With the plugin: exactly one subscriber leaks per cycle, monotonically: 1, 2, 3, ... 10 after invalidate.

Leak point: `packages/core/src/plugin/promise.ts` line 93, `subscribe: () => Stream.toAsyncIterable(host.event.subscribe().pipe(Stream.map(wireEvent)))`. The subscription's lifetime is owned by the async iterator, not the plugin generation, so when a location generation is torn down the plugin's subscriber survives on the global unbounded PubSub. Nothing closes it: the detached loop keeps pulling, so the subscription stays registered on the global PubSub for the life of the process even though its location generation is gone.

This lines up with the report, with one caveat on what's actually reproduced: the harness measures subscriber accumulation, not CPU or RSS. The accumulation is deterministic. The rest follows from it: each leaked subscription stays live and its detached loop keeps draining, so every published event is delivered to and processed by all accumulated generations. The cost is per-event fan-out across N live subscriptions plus the retained fibers and iterators, not an undrained queue backlog. A fresh process has none of this, which is consistent with a clean run staying under 1 percent.

Fix direction I would propose: tie the promise bridge event subscription to the plugin generation scope so teardown interrupts the stream even when the plugin never calls `return()` on the iterator. Happy to open a PR for this referencing this issue.

Repro harness (test file plus a small fixture plugin) available on request; it is 60 lines against `packages/core/test`.

I checked both suggestions. #37946 starts from an already completed errored turn with structural parts and concerns strict-provider serialization; #38270 targets that path. #33687 has an error plus tool state and asks whether provider finish should become `error`. This issue is the earlier scaffold state: zero parts, no error, no finish, and no completion timestamp after setup fails. The fix intentionally leaves `finish` provider-owned while recording an error and completion.

The root cause of this problem is `Bun`. When creating a `Bun Worker` within the same long-running `OpenCode` process, a new .so file is also generated. All these duplicate files are the same `libopentui.so`, each approximately 14 MB in size. It may not increase for a long time when idle; it tends to grow in batches during frequent streaming output, code block, highlighting, or plugin activities.
